sub_questions.question: Is there a way to test what the knowledge base will retrieve before plugging it into a live app?

claims.claim: A Hit Testing panel exists on the dataset page that can be used to test retrieval before publishing an app.
claims.guide_evidence: the **Hit Testing** / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page lets a builder type a sample query

claims.claim: Typing a sample query shows exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores.
claims.guide_evidence: see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

claims.claim: This can be done without running the full app.
claims.guide_evidence: without needing to run the full app

claims.claim: Hit Testing is a good way to sanity-check chunking and indexing choices before wiring the dataset into a retrieval node.
claims.guide_evidence: lets a builder type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

evaluation.rationale: The answer accurately describes the Hit Testing panel on the dataset page, matching the guide: sample query, retrieved chunks, similarity scores, no need to run the full app. The remark about sanity-checking chunking and indexing choices is a reasonable inference from what the panel shows. It is complete, appropriately scoped, and professional.
